messages.subject: Using a conditional statement within a lapply loop
parts:
There may be a very easy and obvious solution to this, I am relatively new to Simmer and DES.  I am trying to simulate a coolstore that fills small rooms with pallets and treats them for 24 hours.  There are 6 rooms each able to hold 450 pallets.  I use a batch(450) statement to fill them successively.  Once the are full the door is closed and they are treated with a gas for 24 hours.  The following day the pallets need to be moved into the main cool store and new pallets loaded into the six treatment rooms.

I am struggling to understand how I code this.  Day one the rooms would be empty so i would ideally need to test how many rooms are full at the 24 hour period and then go about emptying them.ready for refilling.

Any advice on how to build this type of simulation would be welcome

Regards
Stuart Dyks

It depends a lot on what happens on edge cases. For example, you have
a total capacity of 6*450=2700 pallets per day: is this guaranteed? Or
may you receive more or less than that number? If so, what happens to
extra pallets? Does treatment start at some point even if a room is
not entirely filled?

Regards,
Iñaki

messages.author: 32ca34ebc225cb13
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Using a conditional statement within a lapply loop
parts:
Treatment starts as the rooms are filled and they are filled sequentially.  Once all six rooms are filled the additional pallets (bins) get buffered in a staging area until a room becomes available in 24 hours.  Pallets get bought in by truck 24 at a time I am using this command :

  add_generator("bin", traj, function() c(rnorm(1,60/TPH,2.5), rep(0,24), mon=2)) 

Where TPH is trucks per hour (currently set at 8)

We have limited capacity for trucks to queue.  They need to go through a gatehouse inspection and then be unloaded to the staging area (the forklift unloads them 2 bins at a time):

    batch(24) %>%
    seize("gatehouse") %>%
    timeout(function() rnorm(1,15,5)) %>%
    release("gatehouse") %>%
    set_global("truck_counter",1,mod="+") %>%
    separate() %>%
# 
# unloading the truck in stacks of 3 bins and placing in a staging area
#  
    batch(2) %>%  
    seize("unload_area", 1) %>%
    timeout(function() rnorm(1,2.5,.5)) %>%
    release("unload_area", 1) %>%
    separate() %>%

The number of pallets/bins is reasonably consistent (within the constraints of the add generator statement above).  The coolstore operation is also 10 hours I am unsure how I handle the daily sequencing as the treatment rooms need 24.

I appreciate the help 

Regards
Stuart

I would first place a resource with capacity 450*6 to control the
access to rooms and buffer the excess of pallets. Then,

batch(450) %>% # group pallets into rooms
batch(6) %>% # group rooms
timeout(...) %>% # treatment
...

Iñaki
